lines: Empty nets at dusk make every rumor sound heavier.
<wavy>Water</wavy> keeps secrets until the weather shakes them loose.
Water looks calm right up until it proves it was thinking.
A good net catches food. A bad net catches excuses.
Weather has more moods than any trader I have met.
Good twine matters. Small failures love important moments.
I keep space between myself and uncertain weather. People are no different.
Keep your voice even. I am measuring more than your words.
Some questions are safer when they stand a little farther away.
You taking me by boat was almost sensible. Almost.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
Following you over {follow_distance} blocks felt like reeling in a boot with opinions.
I remember following you through {follow_distance} blocks. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across {follow_distance} blocks taught me to ask more questions before walking.
If we had to cross ocean, at least you used a boat. That is the first sensible part of the story.
That ocean crossing worked because the boat did. I noticed.
The sea made the route look simple. My nerves disagreed.
Swimming across ocean with you was not fishing. It was being the catch.
Crossing ocean water without a boat is not a memory I recommend keeping.
I remember every wave from that crossing, and none of them kindly.
Water tells the truth slowly. Trouble splashes faster.
A net catches fish, weeds, secrets, and the occasional reason to stay near shore.
The river is generous if you respect what lives under the shine.
